label: Dirichlet Processes
notes: This appendix, printed pages 218 to 224, develops the Dirichlet process, the nonparametric prior over probability measures that powers the book's Bayes chapters. We meet its two faces: the abstract Ferguson definition and the concrete stick-breaking construction, both feeding the manifold mixture models seen earlier.

label: A Prior Over Measures
notes: Parametric priors place mass on a finite-dimensional vector. The Dirichlet process instead places mass on the infinite-dimensional space of probability measures, letting the data decide how many components a density needs. This flexibility is exactly what manifold density estimation demands.

label: Ferguson Definition
notes: Ferguson defines the Dirichlet process by its finite-dimensional marginals: for every measurable partition the vector of assigned masses follows a Dirichlet distribution with parameters alpha times the base measure. Kolmogorov consistency guarantees a genuine random probability measure exists with these marginals.

label: Base Measure and Concentration
notes: Two knobs control the prior. The base measure G-naught is the prior mean, the measure you expect on average. The concentration alpha tunes dispersion: large alpha keeps draws near G-naught, small alpha yields draws concentrated on a few atoms far from the mean.

label: Stick-Breaking Construction
notes: Sethuraman makes the process constructive. Break a unit stick by independent Beta one alpha fractions; each piece is a weight, and atoms drawn from the base measure receive those weights. The resulting random measure is almost surely discrete, a countable sum of weighted point masses.

label: Weights Decay Geometrically
notes: Because each weight multiplies the remaining stick by a Beta fraction, the weights decay geometrically in expectation. A handful of atoms capture most of the mass, so although infinitely many components exist, only finitely many matter for any finite dataset.

label: Polya Urn Predictive
notes: Integrating out the random measure yields the Polya urn predictive rule. A new draw either copies an existing value, with probability proportional to how often it already appeared, or samples a fresh value from the base measure with probability proportional to alpha.

label: Chinese Restaurant Clustering
notes: The same scheme reads as the Chinese restaurant process: customers pick occupied tables in proportion to their crowd size, or start a new table with weight alpha. This rich-get-richer rule induces clustering automatically, the engine behind nonparametric mixture inference.

label: Conjugacy of the Posterior
notes: The Dirichlet process is conjugate. After observing data, the posterior is again a Dirichlet process whose updated base measure blends the prior G-naught with the empirical distribution, and whose concentration grows by the sample size. Posterior simulation stays tractable.

label: DP Mixture Models
notes: A raw Dirichlet draw is discrete, unsuitable for smooth densities. Convolving it with a continuous kernel gives a Dirichlet process mixture: the atoms become component centers and the kernel smooths them. On manifolds these are exactly the mixtures the book uses for shape densities.

label: Why It Matters on Manifolds
notes: The Dirichlet process supplies a prior that adapts component count to data while respecting the support of the space. On shape manifolds the kernel lives intrinsically, so the mixture honors curvature. This appendix is the probabilistic backbone of the book's Bayesian nonparametric inference.
